html:
The Minaret of Jam is a brick tower about 65 metres tall standing alone in a remote mountain valley of Ghor province, in western Afghanistan. It was built around 1190 by the Ghurids.

The Ghurids were a dynasty from these mountains who overthrew the Ghaznavids in the 12th century and conquered north India. The minaret was raised by the sultan Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad, perhaps to mark a victory. It may stand on the site of the lost Ghurid summer capital, Firozkoh, which the Mongols destroyed in the 1220s.

The tower is made entirely of baked brick, covered with patterns, stucco and bands of blue tile. A whole chapter of the Quran, the chapter of Mary, winds around it in Arabic script.

It is the second tallest old brick minaret in the world, after the Qutb Minar in Delhi, which the Ghurids' generals began a few years later and which it probably inspired. Outsiders knew little of it until a French archaeologist reached it in 1957. It became Afghanistan's first UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002 and is listed as in danger, threatened by floods and erosion.
sum: The Minaret of Jam is a brick tower about 65 metres tall standing alone in a remote mountain valley of Ghor province, in western Afghanistan. It was built around 1190 by the Ghurids.
